attention_linear — LLMCORE attend op

• Data kinds: tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.attention_linear(query, key, value, causal: 'bool' = False) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import llmcore; llmcore.attention_linear(query, key, value, causal: 'bool' = False) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsllmcore.get("attention_linear"))

Usage

Attention with the softmax removed → tokens. (QKᵀ)V == Q(KᵀV) — the associative law itself.

Katharopoulos et al. 2020. Removing the softmax lets the associativity of matrix products apply, so without building (T, T) a state of just (d, dv) suffices. It is the same number bracketed differently, so the answers agree (relative difference 7.1e-16), and the cost moves from O(T²d) to O(Td²) — the crossover is at T == d (measured: ratio 0.9 at T=d=64, 14.6 times at T=1024). ★Even at T = 2048 the ratio levels off at 14.4. It does not reach the 32 times the formula predicts — because the quadratic side becomes band(width)-bound.

Args:

query: (T, d) float.

key: (S, d) float.

value: (S, dv) float. With causal=True, S == T.

causal: if True, adds "only what comes before me" through a cumulative state (1 sequential pass, linear time).

Returns:

tokens (T, dv) float: it does not pass through a softmax, so it is not a convex combination with row sums of 1.

Not a substitute for attention_softmax, but a different attention.
